repositoryChecks.name: repository-tests
repositoryChecks.result: 187 tests passed; one existing Starlette httpx deprecation warning

decisions: POST /v1/catalog/ensure is protected by the existing bearer dependency and uses the injected catalog, job repository, launcher, deterministic clock, and configured date-range and wait bounds.
Ensure job IDs are SHA-256 identifiers of the canonical request, so duplicate requests return the same persisted job and do not relaunch work.

The launcher receives an EnsureJob containing the request and calendar-aware actionable gaps; it is invoked without Azure, provider, file-query, or SAS calls. A deployment composition can adapt this seam to the T027 queue sender.
GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} returns the injected JobRecord state and timestamps; unknown jobs use the existing structured API error response.
limitations: The default application launcher is a provider-free no-op. Deployment composition should inject a queue-backed launcher and durable JobRepository.
The launcher wait is bounded by api.ensure_wait_deadline_seconds; work that outlives the deadline remains available through polling.
T043 file query and SAS behavior is intentionally not implemented.
Focused and repository tests use in-memory repositories and a deterministic timezone-aware clock; no Azure, provider, deployment, or network call was made.
The queue-worker test harness now yields during fake lease renewal so the complete repository suite is bounded and green.
Pytest emits the pre-existing FastAPI/httpx StarletteDeprecationWarning from TestClient.
